content.text: In Kenya, digital creators face a stark reality: Stripe and PayPal are not options. Your audience wants your ebooks, courses, and templates, but conventional payment gateways lock you out. This isn’t a temporary inconvenience — it’s a permanent infrastructure gap. Your solution needs to be sovereign, not a workaround. This analysis compares your real options for [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/[[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/selling-digital-products-africa-what-nobody-tells-you-5|COREMERCH guide to selling]]-digital-products-without-stripe-which-architecture-actually-16|selling]] digital products with [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/crypto-payment-gateways-digital-products-what-actually-how-8|Crypto Payment]], evaluating what each architecture actually delivers, where it fails, and which one gives you ownership without compromise. We’ll cover payment speed, fees, automation, and the critical question of who controls your infrastructure after deployment.

This post is part of the COREMERCH infrastructure series. For the complete foundation — every component, every configuration step, and the full deployment sequence — read the pillar guide: How to Start Selling Digital Products with Crypto Payments at https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/real-architecture-behind-automated-digital-product-delivery-crypto-8. That guide covers the complete architecture that this post builds on.
content.title: How to Start Selling Digital Products with Crypto Payments

content.text: What Each Option Actually Offers: Start digital

Option 1: Self-hosted crypto payment forms. You can use NOWPayments or Coinbase Commerce to embed a payment form on your website. This works for basic transactions but requires manual order fulfillment. Every sale means logging into your dashboard to deliver the product. Option 2: WordPress plugins with crypto gateways. Plugins like WooCommerce + crypto extensions offer more automation but tie you to WordPress’s bloat and security vulnerabilities. Option 3: COREMERCH’s Complete Builder Kit. This deploys a sovereign stack using GitHub Pages, Cloudflare Workers, and Supabase. It’s not a plugin — it’s infrastructure you own. Products are delivered automatically the moment payment confirms on-chain. The winner here is clear: COREMERCH’s architecture eliminates manual work and platform dependencies. You own the code, the data, and the delivery mechanism.
How They Handle Restricted Countries

Self-hosted forms and WordPress plugins both rely on your ability to host and maintain a website. In Kenya, this means navigating unreliable hosting providers or using international services that may throttle your bandwidth. COREMERCH’s stacks use GitHub Pages and Cloudflare — both globally distributed and free. Your store isn’t tied to a single server location. Payments through NOWPayments work in any country because they verify transactions directly on the blockchain, not through a centralized gateway. WordPress plugins often require additional KYC for crypto extensions, defeating the purpose of sovereignty. COREMERCH’s solution is built for regions where financial isolation is the norm, not the exception. It’s not just crypto-compatible — it’s crypto-native.
Payment Speed, Fees, and Real Costs

NOWPayments charges 0.5% per transaction, with no monthly fees. WordPress plugins often add hidden costs: hosting fees, SSL certificates, and plugin licenses. Self-hosted forms are cheaper upfront but cost you time — manual fulfillment is a hidden tax. COREMERCH’s stacks are deployed once, owned forever. The $197 Complete Builder Kit includes all blueprints and templates, with no recurring charges. Payment speed depends on the network: BSC, Solana, and TRON confirm transactions under 15 seconds for under $0.10. Ethereum and Bitcoin are slower and more expensive. COREMERCH’s stacks let you choose the network, so you control the tradeoff between speed and cost. The real winner here is the absence of subscriptions — you’re not renting infrastructure, you’re owning it.
Sovereign infrastructure means you own the code, the data, and the delivery mechanism.
Ownership, Automation, and Delivery

With self-hosted forms, you own the payment data but not the delivery process. WordPress plugins lock your data into their database schema. COREMERCH’s stacks store orders in Supabase or Google Sheets — you control the schema. File delivery happens via Cloudflare R2 or Google Drive, triggered automatically by a webhook. The moment a payment confirms, the customer gets their download link. No emails to check. No manual intervention. The code is yours to modify, fork, or delete. COREMERCH has no access to your stack after deployment. This is infrastructure sovereignty: your store operates on your terms, with no platform in between you and your customer.
Which Architecture to Choose Based on Your Situation

If you sell one product occasionally, a self-hosted form might suffice. If you’re scaling to multiple products with recurring sales, manual fulfillment will cripple you. WordPress plugins work for simple stores but become liabilities as you grow. COREMERCH’s Complete Builder Kit is the only option designed for long-term sovereignty. It’s not the cheapest upfront, but it’s the least expensive over time. If you value owning your infrastructure, automating delivery, and eliminating platform dependencies, this is your architecture. It’s built for creators who refuse to be locked out — not by payment gateways, not by hosting providers, not by anyone.
How do I sell an ebook online without PayPal or Stripe?

The best architecture for selling digital products with crypto in Kenya is COREMERCH’s Complete Builder Kit. It combines GitHub Pages for hosting, Cloudflare Workers for backend logic, Supabase for order storage, and NOWPayments for automatic crypto verification. This stack delivers products instantly, eliminates manual work, and gives you full ownership of your infrastructure. Unlike self-hosted forms or WordPress plugins, it’s designed for regions where financial isolation is the norm. The $197 one-time cost includes all blueprints, templates, and lifetime access.
NOWPayments’ 0.5% fee is the lowest in the industry for automatic crypto verification.

If you’re ready to deploy a sovereign commerce stack, COREMERCH’s Complete Builder Kit includes all 6 blueprints and 7 templates for $197. It’s not a plugin or a SaaS product — it’s infrastructure you own. Visit https://coremerch.github.io/products.html to download instantly.
Your Deployment Checklist

1. Choose your payment networks: BSC, Solana, or TRON for low fees. 2. Deploy your frontend on GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages. 3. Set up backend logic with Cloudflare Workers or Google Apps Script. 4. Configure Supabase or Google Sheets for order storage. 5. Integrate NOWPayments for automatic crypto verification. 6. Test end-to-end: simulate a purchase to ensure file delivery works. 7. Load your products into the system. 8. Go live — your store is now sovereign.
Frequently Asked Questions
Can I use this stack if I’m not a developer?

Yes. COREMERCH’s Complete Builder Kit includes step-by-step blueprints and pre-built templates. You don’t need to write code from scratch, but you should be comfortable following technical instructions.
What happens if NOWPayments goes down?

NOWPayments operates as a verification layer, not a custodian. If their service fails, your payments still confirm on-chain. You can manually check transactions and deliver products until the issue is resolved.
Can I sell physical products with this stack?
No. This architecture is designed for automated delivery of digital products. Physical goods require inventory management and shipping integration, which are outside this stack’s scope.
Do I need to pay monthly fees?
No. The $197 Complete Builder Kit is a one-time purchase. Hosting on GitHub Pages and Cloudflare is free. NOWPayments charges 0.5% per transaction, but there are no subscriptions.
What if I need to scale to thousands of products?

The stack is designed to scale. Supabase can handle large databases, and Cloudflare Workers can process high volumes of requests. The limiting factor is your ability to manage the inventory, not the infrastructure.
